summary: Validated the new 'Ordered Execution Check' scoring method for Turtle problems end-to-end. Backend pytest suite /app/backend/tests/test_ordered_execution.py — 7/7 PASS in ~5s covering: (1) POST /api/problems stores scoring_method='ordered_execution' + target_sequence=['forward','right','forward','left','forward']; (2) PUT /api/problems/{id} updates target_sequence and persists via GET; (3) Legacy turtle problem without scoring_method defaults to 'text_match' (backward-compatible); (4) Student POST /api/submissions with correct sequence → score 100 + feedback contains 'Perfect' + turtle_tracking_data.commands_used is a populated list with raw commands like 'forward(50)'; (5) Wrong step 2 (left instead of right) → score 0 + feedback matches exactly 'Step 2 was `left`, try that again and resubmit.'; (6) Too-short (3 commands vs 5 target) → 'Step 4 was `(nothing)`, try that again and resubmit.'; (7) Extra command beyond target → 'Step 6 was `right`, try that again and resubmit.'. Frontend Playwright on /library after admin login: (a) Create-Problem dialog opens, Unit Type=Turtle → the purple 'Scoring Method' panel (data-testid lib-new-scoring-method) IS visible; default value = 'Text Match (default) — compare final output/image'; (b) target-sequence textarea is HIDDEN by default and APPEARS after switching to 'Ordered Execution Check' — data-testid lib-new-target-sequence works. Panel condition (turtle OR block) is present in code at AssignmentLibrary.jsx L2128 & L3512 for Create + Edit dialogs respectively. Edit-dialog testids lib-edit-scoring-method and lib-edit-target-sequence are wired to the same setEditingProblem state and are covered by the PUT persistence backend test. Overall feature works as spec'd.

issues: Field labeled 'Unit Type' (native select data-testid=lib-assignment-type-select) actually controls newProblem.assignment_type — same field is ALSO surfaced as a segmented button group titled 'Assignment Type' further down the form. Two controls for the same value can confuse teachers. Consider consolidating into one control.

action_items: OPTIONAL cleanup: The Create dialog has both a Unit-Type dropdown AND an Assignment-Type segmented button that write to the same `assignment_type` field — consider removing one for clarity.
OPTIONAL: Add data-testid to the 'Add to Library' / 'Save Changes' submit button for the EDIT dialog form; currently only the CREATE dialog submit has data-testid='lib-submit-btn'.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py grade_turtle_submission (L3421) — Ordered Execution branch correctly handles missing target_sequence (empty list) by falling through to legacy grading. Good defensive default.

server.py L4611–4671 — Blockly turtle short-circuit for ordered_execution reuses grade_turtle_submission — clean DRY approach. Score gating is base_score>=70 for is_passing but Ordered Execution returns 0 or 100 only, so is_passing correctly aligns.
AssignmentLibrary.jsx L2135 / L3519 — `value={newProblem.scoring_method || 'text_match'}` handles legacy problems w/ null field, good backward-compat.
AssignmentLibrary.jsx L2162 / L3546 — target_sequence stored as `.split('\n').map(trim).filter(Boolean)` — silently drops empty lines. Reasonable UX.
server.py L1245 — teacher-login always resets user.role='teacher' on login. This means the switch-role trick in test-only paths (student mode) is reset each time. Fine for prod, but noted.

success_rate.frontend: Create-dialog UI fully verified (4/4 checks); Edit-dialog covered by backend PUT persistence test + code review of mirror UI

context_for_next_testing_agent: Ordered-Execution scoring uses turtle_tracking_data.commands_used (list of raw 'forward(50)' style strings) from /app/backend/turtle_sim.py get_tracking_data(). Feedback format is EXACTLY 'Step {N} was `{method}`, try that again and resubmit.' (with backticks) — verify this pattern in any UI that surfaces feedback so student sees the correct message. For lesson-based submissions, use assignment_id starting with 'lesson_' to bypass classroom-enrollment checks — very useful for backend testing. Teacher-login endpoint resets role to 'teacher' every time; to test student flows on same account, call POST /api/auth/switch-role AFTER login (reuses session token). The pytest suite creates a module-scoped fixture that creates the OE test problem BEFORE the student_headers fixture triggers role switch — critical ordering.
rca of the issue: N/A — brand new feature, no bug. All acceptance criteria met.
